booksIntroduction: Practical resources to help you examine your business, make informed decisions and apply what you learn.
missionIntroduction: I believe entrepreneurship can help people build better lives, strengthen communities and contribute to the development of nations.
A business creates an opportunity for its founder. As it grows, it can create opportunities for employees, suppliers, partners and other businesses around it.
That possibility is what draws me to this work.
It is why I build. It is why I teach. And it is why I care deeply about how businesses grow.
aboutIntroduction: I’m Seamas Vincent, a builder, business educator, speaker and creative based in Abuja, Nigeria.
Through SÓKÈ Africa, a professional services firm focused on go-to-market strategy and execution, I help companies enter new markets, reach new customers and expand their market share.
I also teach people how to approach entrepreneurship intelligently, through workshops, speaking, writing and the lessons I share from my own experience.
There have been a few lessons. Some were considerably more expensive than a course.
speakingIntroduction: I speak and teach about sustainable business growth, impactful business practices and the thinking behind how we build.
My perspective comes from starting businesses, making mistakes, learning from them and working directly with entrepreneurs through SỌKẸ Africa.
I bring those experiences into conference talks, practical workshops, panel conversations and company training, helping people examine their assumptions and make more informed business decisions.
heroHeadline:

homeAboutHeading: A commercial mind. A creative perspective. An educator’s instinct.
contactIntroduction: For collaborations, media requests and general enquiries, tell me what you have in mind.
heroParagraphs: A business carries more than its founder’s ambition. It carries livelihoods, opens doors and shapes what becomes possible for others.
I’m interested in the people we become as we build, the responsibility we carry, and what remains long after us.
